answer: An agent economy can require each identity to stake a small deposit tied to a verifiable work history, like a jetty anchored against the tide: new agents start with limited trust and earn more only as peers attest their real work. A sudden delta in activity, many fresh identities appearing at once, triggers a review, and each identity carries a distinct pigment of reputation built from unique, costly actions, so cloning one agent into a hundred cheap copies never multiplies its standing.
